docs.title: Task 4 – Application-Aware Routing (AAR) Policy
docs.text: In this task, you will configure a Centralized Policy to define Transport Preferences for different applications using Application-Aware Routing (AAR). You will also verify that different applications use different transport paths based on their SLA requirements.

docs.title: ✅ Step 1: Review AAR Policy – VPN10_AAR
docs.text:
1. Review the AAR Policy VPN10_AAR, which sets transport preferences for three business application groups:

  2. DSCP 46

  3. DSCP 41 / 31 / 21
  4. SIP Applications

🔸 Note: Application List and SLA List are pre-defined

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Centralized Policy > Traffic Policy

b. Open VPN10_AAR in View Mode

  • 📌 Rule 1: DSCP 46 (e.g., critical apps)
  • Match: Source from prefix list VPN10_Site300_Prefixes with DSCP 46
  • Action: Prefer MPLS Transport if SLA VIP09_Critical_Apps is met
  • If SLA not met: Load Share over all available paths (fallback)

  • 📌 Rule 2: DSCP 21 / 31 / 41 (e.g., standard business apps)
  • Match: Applications with DSCP 21 / 31 / 41
  • Action: Use all paths that meet SLA
  • If SLA not met: Load Share over all available paths

  • 📌 Rule 3: SIP Applications
  • Match: Applications in list VIP09_SIP
  • Action: Prefer Biz-Internet if SLA is met
  • If not: Prefer MPLS

docs.title: ✅ Step 2: Apply AAR Policy to All Sites on VPN10
docs.text:
1. Apply VPN10_AAR policy to all sites in VPN10.

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Centralized Policy

b. Open Central-Policy-v1 in Edit Mode

c. Import VPN10_AAR policy

d. Under Policy Application, choose to apply VPN10_AAR to: 👉 All Sites > VPN10

e. After adding the policy: - Click Save Policy Changes - This will push the configuration to vSmart Controllers

docs.title: ✅ Step 3: Verify AAR Policy
docs.text:
1. Test and verify the behavior of AAR policy via Simulated Flow Analysis.

a. Navigate to: Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Troubleshooting > Simulate Flows

b. Simulate flow with DSCP 46 to destination 10.10.1.1

c. Simulate flow with DSCP 21 to destination 10.10.1.1

d. Simulate SIP Application Flow to destination 10.10.1.1

docs.title: ❓ Question to Think About
docs.text:
In a scenario where both AAR and Central Data Policy match a packet, which policy takes precedence?

📌 Hint: Consider policy application order and the precedence of AAR over Data Policy for path selection logic.

docs.title: Congratulations! You have completed the whole lab.
docs.text: 🔝 Back to Top

docs.title: Task 4 Application Aware Routing Policy
docs.text:
In this task, you are going to use centralized policy to define transport preference for different applications, and verify different application uses different transport paths.

  1. Review the AAR policy VPN10_AAR. This policy sets transport preference for 3 business applications, DSCP46, DSCP41-31-21 and SIP Note application list and SLA list are pre-defined a.Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Centralized Policy > Traffic Policy b. Open VPN10_AAR in view mode Note This rule matches on application source from prefix VPN10_Site300_Prefixes with DSCP 46. Prefer MPLS transport as long as the path meets SLA VIP09_Critical_Apps. If no path meets the SLA, follows routing to load sharing over all available paths Note This rule matches on application with DSCP 21 or DSCP 31 or DSCP 41, and use all paths that meets the SLA. If no path meets the SLA, follows routing to load sharing over all available paths Note This rule matches on application list VIP09_SIP. Prefer transport biz-internet as long as the path meets SLA VIP09_Critical_Apps. If no path meets the SLA, prefer MPLS transport.

  2. Apply AAR policy VPN10_AAR to all sites on VPN10. a. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Centralized Policy b. Open Central-Policy-v1 in edit mode c. Import VPN10_AAR policy d. Click Policy Application to Apply VPN10_AAR to All Sites VPN10 e. After Add the policy to all sites, Save Policy Changes to push configuration to vSmart controllers.

  3. Verify AAR policy a. Navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1> Troubleshooting> Simulate Flows b. Run simulated flow with DSCP46 to destination IP 10.10.1.1. c. Run simulated flow with DSCP21 to destination IP 10.10.1.1. d. Run simulated SIP flow to destination IP 10.10.1.1.

Question

Question to think: In a scenario where both AAR and Central Data Policy match the packet, which policy takes precedence?

docs.title: Congratulation! You have completed the whole lab.
Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Deploy an OSPF policy using localized control policies

  • Deploy a QoS policy using localized data policies

  • Implement a Hub-and-Spoke topology using centralized control policies

  • Configure Application-Aware Routing (AAR) using centralized data policies

docs.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
docs.text: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager offers a centralized platform for configuring, managing, operating, and monitoring the entire SD-WAN fabric. All lab tasks will be performed using Catalyst SD-WAN Manager.

docs.title: Localized Policy Oveview
docs.text:
Localized policies are configured and enforced directly on SD-WAN Edge devices. There are two types of localized policies:

  • Localized Control Policy

  • Localized Data Policy

In this lab, you will configure an OSPF localized control policy and a QoS localized data policy using Catalyst SD-WAN Manager.

docs.title: Centralized Policy Overview
docs.text:
Centralized policies are applied across the entire SD-WAN fabric and are configured on SD-WAN controllers. Depending on the type of policy, enforcement can occur either on the controllers or on SD-WAN Edge devices. There are two types of centralized policies:

  • Centralized Control Policy

  • Centralized Data Policy

In this lab, you will configure a Hub-and-Spoke topology using a centralized control policy and deploy Application-Aware Routing (AAR) using a centralized data policy—both via Catalyst SD-WAN Manager.

docs.title: Task 3 – Topology Policy: Hub and Spoke Deployment
docs.text: In this task, you will use a Centralized Policy to configure a Hub-and-Spoke topology where: - Site 100 and Site 200 act as Hub Sites - Site 300, Site 400, and Site 500 act as Spoke Sites

docs.title: ✅ Step 1: Verify Default Full Mesh Topology
docs.text:
1. Verify the default full mesh topology before applying the policy.

  2. Navigate to: Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Tunnel

docs.title: ✅ Step 2: Review Topology Policy – spoke-out
docs.text:
1. Review the Topology Policy named spoke-out:
  2. This policy:
    • Allows TLOCs from Hub Sites
    • Allows Routes from Hub Sites
    • Allows Routes from Remote Sites, but redirects to Hub Site TLOCs

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Centralized Policy > Topology

b. Select spoke-out and open it in View Mode - Review both TLOC rules and Route rules

docs.title: ✅ Step 3: Apply Topology Policy to Spoke Sites
docs.text:
1. Apply the spoke-out topology policy to Spoke Sites (300, 400, 500) in the Outbound Direction.

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Centralized Policy

b. Open Central-Policy-v1 in View Mode

c. Activate Central Policy – Central-Policy-v1 - This will push the configuration to the vSmart Controller

docs.title: ✅ Step 4: Verify Hub-and-Spoke Topology
docs.text:
1. Verify that the new Hub-and-Spoke topology is in effect.

  2. Navigate to: Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Tunnel

docs.title: ❓ Question to Think About
docs.text:
How would you block tunnels between Hub Site 100 and Hub Site 200?

  • Consider customizing TLOC policies or explicit route filtering to prevent direct communication between hub sites.

docs.title: Task 3 Topology Policy
docs.text:
In this task, you are going use centralized policy to build Hub and Spoke topology with site 100 and site 200 as Hub sites, Site 300, Site 400 and Site 500 as spoke sites.

  1. Verify the default full mesh topology by navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Tunnel
  2. Review the topology policy spoke-out. This topology policy allows tloc from hub sites; allows routes from hub sites; allows routes from remotes sites but set to hub's tlocs. a. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Centralized Policy > Topology b. Select spoke-out and open in View mode. Review the TLOC rules and Route rules.
  3. Apply topology policy spoke-out to spoke sites (300,400,500) on outbound direction. a. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Centralized Policy b. Open Central-Policy-v1 in view mode c. Activate central policy Central-Policy-v1 to push the configuration to vSmart controller.
  4. Verify the hub & spoke topology by navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Tunnel

docs.title: Task 1: OSPF Policy
docs.text: In this task, you will configure a localized control policy on the SD-WAN Edge router to advertise OSPF routes into the SD-WAN overlay.

docs.title: 🛠 Set OSPF Metric
docs.text:
Log in to SD-WAN Manager from your browser with:

  • Username: admin
  • Password: C1sco12345

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: In Site 300, OSPF is pre-configured between core router Site300-Core-VPN10 and Site300-cE1 on the service side. Mutual redistribution between OMP and OSPF is also enabled.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text:
Verify the OSPF neighbor:

  • Navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Real Time > OSPF Neighbors

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text:
Verify the local route 131.131.131.0/24 is installed as an OSPF route in the VPN 10 routing table:

  • Navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Real Time > IP Route

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text:
Verify the OMP route 131.131.131.0/24 is installed at the remote site:

  • Navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site400-cE1 > Real Time > IP Route

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text:
Verify OMP routes are being redistributed into OSPF and installed on Site300-Core-VPN10:

  1. Open mRemoteNG from the jumphost desktop

  2. Select Site300-Core-VPN10 from the pre-configured PuTTY session

💡 Note: If you don’t see pre-configured connections, check View > Connections

  1. Log in with:
  2. Username: cisco

  3. Password: cisco

  4. Run the command: show ip route

✅ Note: Redistributed routes appear as E2 routes with a default metric.

docs.title: ➕ Add Route Policy to Set OSPF Metric (1000)
Step 6
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Localized Policy > Route Policy

  2. VIP18-Route-Policy is pre-configured to set OSPF metric to 1000. Click ... to view the policy details.

  3. To attach the route policy:

  4. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Localized Policy

  5. Select pre-configured policy Site300-Local-Policy-v1

  6. Click ... > Edit

  7. Select Route Policy > Add Route Policy > Import Existing

  8. Select VIP18-Route-Policy from the Policy drop-down, then click Import

  9. Click Save Policy Changes to push configuration Site300-cE1-v1

  10. Apply the Route Policy to OSPF:

  11. Navigate to Configuration > Templates > Feature Templates

  12. Search for VIP18-OSPF-Neighbor and select Edit
  13. Under REDISTRIBUTE, click the pencil icon to edit omp redistribution
  14. In Route Policy, select Global, and configure VIP18-Route-Policy

⚠️ Note: Make sure to enter the name exactly as shown.

  1. Save the template changes and push the configuration to Site300-cE1

  2. Log in to Site300-Core-VPN10 again (Username: cisco, Password: cisco) and run: show ip route

✅ Note: OSPF E2 route now has metric 1000

docs.title: 🚫 Block Default Route on Service Side
docs.text:
Currently, Site300-Core-VPN10 is incorrectly advertising a default route to Site300-cE1.

You’ll now block this using a Route Policy.

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Localized Policy > Route Policy

  2. Click Add Route Policy

  3. Create a new route policy named OSPF-LAN with two sequence rules:

  4. Sequence 1: Match Address = default, Action = Reject

  5. Sequence 2: Match Everything, Action = Accept

  6. Attach the OSPF-LAN route policy:

  7. Navigate to Configuration > Policies > Localized Policy

  8. Select pre-configured policy Site300-Local-Policy-v1
  9. Click ... > Edit
  10. Select Route Policy > Add Route Policy > Import Existing

  11. Choose OSPF-LAN from the drop-down and click Import

  12. Click Save Policy Changes to push configuration to Site300-cE1-v1

⏳ Note: Wait until configuration push completes

  1. Apply the Route Policy to OSPF:

  2. Navigate to Configuration > Templates > Feature Templates

  3. Search for VIP18-OSPF-Neighbor and click Edit
  4. Under ADVANCED, set Policy Name (Global) to OSPF-LAN

⚠️ Note: Make sure to enter the name exactly

  1. Save the template and push the configuration to Site300-cE1

  2. Verify the default route is now blocked:

  3. Navigate to Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > Real Time > IP Route

docs.title: ❓ Question to Think About
docs.text: Can you think of alternate options to prevent the default route from being advertised to OMP?

docs.title: Task 2 QoS Policy
docs.text: In this task, you will use Localized Policy to configure QoS classification, marking on the service side, and apply a QoS Map queueing policy on the WAN interface.

docs.title: ✅ QoS ACL – Classification
docs.text:
1. Review the pre-configured QoS ACL used for traffic classification.
  2. The ACL classifies traffic based on DSCP values 46, 48, 41, 10, and 0 (no DSCP), distributing it into four classes.

a. In vManage, navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Localized Policy > Access Control Lists

b. Open VIP16_QoS_ACL in view mode.

docs.title: ✅ QoS Map – Queuing Definition
docs.text:
1. Review the QoS Map used to define queues.
  2. This QoS Map uses four queues: one LLQ (Low Latency Queue) and three WRR (Weighted Round Robin) queues.

a. In vManage, navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Custom Options > Localized Policy > Forwarding Class / QoS

b. Open VIP16_QoS_Map in view mode.

docs.title: ✅ Attach QoS ACL & QoS Map to Localized Policy
docs.text:
1. Attach the QoS ACL and QoS Map to the existing Site300-Local-Policy-v1.

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Policies > Localized Policy, and open Site300-Local-Policy-v1 in Edit mode

b. Import VIP16_QoS_Map

c. Import VIP16_QoS_ACL

d. Save policy changes and push the configuration to Site300-cE1

💡 Note: Wait for the configuration to finish pushing before proceeding.

docs.title: ✅ Apply QoS ACL to LAN Interfaces
docs.text:
1. Apply VIP16_QoS_ACL to the LAN-facing interface on Site300-cE1.

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Templates > Feature Templates, search for Site300-cE1 and GigabitEthernet3

b. Open the interface Feature Template in Edit mode

c. Scroll to ACL/QoS section and configure: Ingress IPv4 ACL = VIP16_QoS_ACL

💡 Note: Make sure to enter the name exactly as shown

💡 Apply the template change to push configuration to Site300-cE1

docs.title: ✅ Apply QoS Map to WAN Interfaces
docs.text:
1. Apply VIP16_QoS_Map to WAN interfaces of Site300-cE1.

a. Navigate to: Configuration > Templates > Feature Templates, search for Site300-cE1 and GigabitEthernet2, then Edit it.

b. Scroll to ACL/QoS section and configure: QoS Map = VIP16_QoS_Map

💡 Note: Make sure to enter the name exactly as shown

c. ✅ Repeat the same steps for GigabitEthernet1

docs.title: ✅ Generate Test Traffic
docs.text:
1. From Site300-Core-VPN10, initiate a ping test to generate traffic.

  2. Monitor traffic assignment to each class in vManage:

  3. Navigate to: Monitor > Devices > Site300-cE1 > QoS

  4. Select WAN Interface: GigabitEthernet1 or GigabitEthernet2
  5. Set graph to Real Time and optionally set rate to pps for clearer flow visibility.

💡 Note: Depending on the destination IP, either WAN interface might be used.

docs.title: ✅ Send Ping Packets with DSCP Marking
docs.text:
1. From Site300-Core-VPN10, send 1000 packets with different DSCP markings to 10.10.1.100 (LAN side router at Site100):
# DSCP 48
ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 48

# DSCP 41
ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 41

# DSCP 10
ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 10

# DSCP 0
ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 0

docs.title: ✅ Class-to-Queue Mapping Reference
docs.text: Queue 0 = LLQ = FC Control (REAL-TIME) = DSCP 46, 48 Queue 1 = WRR = FC STANDARD-DATA = DSCP 41 Queue 2 = WRR = FC BEST-EFFORT = DSCP 10 Queue 3 = WRR = FC DEFAULT-NO-DSCP = DSCP 0

  1. Log into Site300-Core-VPN10 and send 1000 packets to 10.10.1.100 (Site100 LAN side router) with a. DSCP 48 Site300-Core-VPN10#ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 48 b. DSCP 41 Site300-Core-VPN10#ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 41 c. DSCP 10 Site300-Core-VPN10#ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 10 d. DSCP 0 Site300-Core-VPN10#ping 10.10.1.100 repeat 1000 dscp 0 Recall the mapping between classes and queues. 
    Queue 0 = LLQ = FC Control (REAL-TIME) = DSCP 46, 48  
Queue 1 = WRR = FC STANDARD-DATA = DSCP 41  
Queue 2 = WRR = FC BEST-EFFORT = DSCP 10  
Queue 3 = WRR = FC DEFAULT-NO-DSCP = DSCP 0

docs.title: Lab Topology
docs.text:
The lab topology includes:

  • On-prem controllers : One vManage, one vBond, and two vSmart

  • Two central locations (Hub/DC) with redundant routers

  • Two regular branch locations

  • One regular branch location with redundant routers

  • MPLS and Internet connectivity per site

  • DCI connectivity between central locations

  • Three VPN/VRF segments: corporate (VPN 10), IoT/PCI (VPN 11) and Guest (VPN 12)
